stories.title: ILS and alternative capital expanding footprint into DUAE market: AM Best
stories.summary: AM Best has said alternative capital and insurance-linked securities (ILS) are increasingly entering the delegated underwriting authority enterprise (DUAE) space. DUAEs are using sidecars, catastrophe bonds and collateralized reinsurance to secure capacity when insurers step back, and the segment posted its fifth consecutive year of double-digit premium growth, outpacing the broader U.S. property and casualty industry. AM Best has kept its stable outlook for the segment and expects premium growth to moderate, with private equity capital continuing to flow in and smaller, less-differentiated players likely to become acquisition targets.
stories.why_it_matters: Capacity is becoming partner specific, so DUAEs with volatile results may struggle to secure backing while disciplined ones gain access to alternative capital.

stories.title: Atrium and CRC launch Fractal Re II third-party capital backed reinsurance portfolio at Lloyd’s
stories.summary: Atrium, a Lloyd's underwriter that is part of the CRC Group, has launched Fractal Re II, a third-party capital backed reinsurance portfolio. It covers a diversified portfolio of property, specialty and casualty risks underwritten via Atrium's Syndicate 2026, and succeeds the Fractal Re I transaction. The earlier Fractal Re arrangement in 2024 was a quota share sidecar under Bermuda vehicle Fractal Re Ltd, which secured $270 million of collateralized reinsurance capacity for certain casualty risk focused programs.
stories.why_it_matters: It shows how a wholesale and program group can use a Lloyd's syndicate to tap third-party capital for reinsurance capacity.

stories.title: Tech stocks surge as Jensen Huang is reinstated as Nvidia chief executive
stories.summary: Tech stocks surged on Wall Street on Monday after Nvidia said it was reinstating co-founder Jensen Huang as chief executive. Nvidia's shares rose 33 per cent after the open in New York, following a 21 per cent loss last week, and the stock had lost $2.5 trillion in value since its October peak. The Nasdaq 100 rose 7.1 per cent and the S&P 500 rose 4.8 per cent in early trading, while Anthropic shares fell 1.8 per cent to $87.2 after the open, extending an 8.5 per cent loss on Friday.
stories.why_it_matters: Nvidia's weight in US indices means one leadership decision moved the whole market, showing how concentrated AI-linked risk appetite has become.

stories.title: The Download: AI’s judgment problem and carbon removal’s crop threat
stories.summary: The AI evaluation nonprofit METR has updated its widely shared time horizon plot, which tests models on a large suite of tasks. The new version adds more open-ended tasks, such as designing AI evaluations and scoring philosophical arguments, and models struggled with these. METR finds some capabilities are improving exponentially, but models are less good at tasks that require judgment than at coding.
stories.why_it_matters: Weakness at judgment-based tasks could limit how far AI can automate research and development, which matters for assumptions about the pace of AI progress.

stories.title: Philip R. Lane: Climate change and monetary policy
Wild stock market swings: will I lose money, and is there anything I can do?
stories.summary: Global stock markets have been volatile, with rapid rallies and punishing sell-offs. Investors have shown signs in recent weeks of getting cold feet over the outlook for AI companies and have been selling technology stocks. On Friday stock markets around the world tumbled and the US Nasdaq closed 5% below its mark on 1 January, a day after the AI company Anthropic launched on to the market and had a record-breaking first day.
stories.why_it_matters: Doubts over AI company prospects are driving sharp falls in tech shares, which can hit portfolios and pensions with large exposure to global or US tech indices.
stories.access_note: A UK retail investor can get exposure to global and technology shares through equity index funds and ETFs, individual shares, options, and leveraged products such as spread bets and CFDs.

stories.title: Ukraine takes the war against Russia far from its borders
stories.summary: Ukraine's Security Service, the SBU, said its forces on Sunday sank the Russian corvette Merkury anchored in the Libyan port of Benghazi. The Angara, a Russian dry cargo vessel that Kyiv claimed was carrying weapons, was also hit, and it is the first time Ukraine has claimed credit for such a distant strike. Separately, Finland's defence ministry said a Russian-flagged cargo ship was damaged by a drone in the Gulf of Finland on Saturday, and Finnish authorities said Ukraine carried out the attack, which Ukraine has not admitted.
stories.why_it_matters: Ukraine is widening its pressure on Moscow beyond the front line and refineries, which raises the risk of diplomatic blowback and of further disruption to shipping.

stories.title: Macron moves to ‘trap’ successors with new budget rule
stories.summary: President Emmanuel Macron is pushing to put strict deficit rules into France's constitution before he leaves office in May. France has nearly €3.6 trillion in debt, equal to 119% of gross domestic product, and a budget deficit projected at 5.4% of GDP this year. A constitutional change needs a referendum or a three-fifths majority of both chambers, and a former parliamentary aide said it could pass by as many as 20 votes if centrists and conservatives backed it and Marine Le Pen's National Rally abstained.
stories.why_it_matters: A constitutional deficit rule would bind the next government's fiscal policy, and the vote would force presidential candidates such as Le Pen and Edouard Philippe to take a side on French public finances.

stories.title: Russian warship hit by Ukrainian drones in Libya, Zelensky says
stories.summary: A Russian warship has been hit by Ukrainian drones in Libya, according to Zelensky. The Kremlin warns of an "escalation of tensions in the region". It declines to comment directly on the attacks in Libya.
stories.why_it_matters: Attacks reaching Libya would widen the area where the Russia-Ukraine war is fought, and the Kremlin's warning points to rising regional tension.

stories.title: Ukraine shares video of strikes on Russian ships off Libya
stories.summary: Ukraine has shared video of strikes on Russian ships off Libya. President Zelensky said a Russia warship was sunk. He also said a Russian cargo ship was hit.
stories.why_it_matters: Strikes on both a warship and a cargo ship far from Ukraine suggest Russian naval and commercial vessels may be exposed well beyond the front line.

market_idea.title: Hedging a tech-heavy portfolio against a Nasdaq sell-off
market_idea.what_the_trade_is: The view is that tech and AI shares could fall further after the Nasdaq closed 5% below its 1 January mark. The aim is to limit losses on existing tech holdings rather than to exit them.
market_idea.how_it_is_expressed: A hedge is a position that gains when the thing you own falls, such as a put option or a short index position sized against the tech holdings. It offsets part of the loss without selling the underlying shares.
market_idea.retail_access: A UK retail investor could use index options, or short positions through spread bets or CFDs on a tech index. Spread bets and CFDs are leveraged and use margin, so losses can exceed the initial deposit, and options cost a premium that is lost if the hedge is not needed.
market_idea.what_makes_it_work: Tech shares need to keep falling by more than the cost of the hedge, so that its gains offset losses on the portfolio.
market_idea.what_breaks_it: If tech shares rebound sharply, the hedge loses money or its premium expires worthless, which leaves the investor paying for protection they did not need.
market_idea.disclaimer: An explanation of a trade in the news, not a recommendation.

quiz.question: What do DUAEs with volatile results risk, as capacity becomes tied to specific partners?
options: Struggling to find capital backers
Being forced into sidecar structures
Losing their stable outlook rating
Facing caps on premium growth
quiz.explanation: When capacity depends on partner relationships, erratic performers are less attractive to backers, while disciplined ones gain access to capital.
quiz.evidence: Capacity is becoming partner specific, so DUAEs with volatile results may struggle to secure backing while disciplined ones gain access to alternative capital.

quiz.question: A investor holds many tech shares and buys a hedge instead of selling them. What would make the hedge pay off?
options: Tech prices stay flat while the option nears expiry
Tech prices fall only slightly, less than the hedge costs
Tech prices drop by more than the hedge costs
Tech prices rise sharply and the hedge is kept
quiz.explanation: The hedge only comes out ahead when the decline in tech shares is bigger than what the protection cost to buy.
quiz.evidence: Tech shares need to keep falling by more than the cost of the hedge, so that its gains offset losses on the portfolio.
